That's all for theory. Would you like to continue watching?
So you knew I was here.
Huh? When did you get here?
A while ago. But Albedo sounded like he was working on his thesis defense back there. Back in Sumeru, you can end a person's whole career by interrupting them mid-speech.
Very thoughtful of you — I'm truly touched. Could I ask you to lend me a hand?
With what?
A little test. Try using Anemo to unleash a concentrated assault with circular blades, with the goal of breaking through at a singular point.
Nice! This time, it tore through the field!
Tremendous. This is a major breakthrough.
Should we go through?
We probably shouldn't risk having mutually antagonistic energies in such close proximity... Durin, you stay here and watch the entrance. Hat Guy and I will go in to investigate.
Sounds sensible to me. Keep your eyes peeled, Durin.
Don't worry, I've got this. You two be careful in there. Just give me the signal if you need help, and I'll dive right in.
What do you mean, "signal"?

It's based on a new alchemical concoction I developed last month. When two bottles of it are smashed on the ground together, they emit a blinding burst of light. If it comes to that, remember to shield your eyes with your hat.
Glad I asked. Thanks for the heads-up.
They have no heartbeat and they're not breathing... We can only assume they're dead. But there are no visible wounds...
Also, there's an animal squatting next to each body.
...It's watching us. That's not an animal's gaze.
What are you trying to tell us?
Doesn't seem eager to talk... I guess maybe it is just an animal after all.
Let's keep looking around.
Same situation everywhere. Not a living soul in sight... just countless bodies with animals standing watch over them.
Well... I think we can safely rule out the possibility that they're all pets.
...Is skirting around the topic your way of showing consideration for other people's feelings?
Just being cautious. I don't doubt that you can handle the truth.
Please... help us... Please...
What happened here?
...I don't know... Suddenly, everyone collapsed... Then my line of sight got... lower...
I still... have some of my senses left... I gotta... get out of here... I... Ah, aah...
*cheep*
It looks like there's a huge experiment going on inside this energy field.
Maybe each energy field is its own giant experiment... Ugh. Vile.
He's swapping human minds with those of animals... Even without the other circumstances, this would still be an extremely radical experiment.

Those people may have lost their sense of selves, but they are not fully animals either. If they were, they would have left — but instead, their instincts are driving them to remain by their dead bodies.
We should go. No sense in sticking around here longer than we need to.
Agreed.

dialogue.section: Albedo, Lauma, Nefer, Durin, Nicole, The Doctor, Dodocommunication Device

dialogue.t: You're back! Everything okay?
We saw some things that take a strong stomach. Otherwise, we're fine.
We should share our findings with the others.
Dodo! Dodo! Dodoco!
Yes? Who is it?
Miss Nefer, it's me, Albedo.
We've found a way to break through the energy fields. With enough control, it's possible to tear them open using elemental energy.
Also, we managed to take a look inside. Dottore is carrying out his cruel experiments on an immense scale. Any residents who have failed to evacuate in time will likely meet a grisly end.
Sounds like he's living down to our expectations.
Might I ask how things are proceeding on your end?
I'm just about to get started. I'll be in touch once I have a result.
Understood. Stay safe.
I will.
Well, Nefer, I'll link up with you once my tasks are complete.
What makes you think I'd need you to do that?
I'll need it. And considering the way you approach certain matters, I think you'll be better off with me present.
Hmph.
Let's begin. Entering simulation mode...
(A vast wasteland. Is this {NICKNAME}'s inner world?)
(...I was expecting something more vibrant, to be honest.)
(Wait. Someone's there...)

dialogue.sit: In that case, I'll look at it with you.
I want to know all about everything you've seen and experienced.
...Is there somewhere I should return to? Or should I stay here and be the hero everyone says I am?
I don't dislike my current life. Roaming the land, fighting battles, accomplishing missions, earning a living, looking after Paimon... It's not so bad.
I guess the only thing that's missing is that... you're not here with me.

dialogue.t: (This is the conscious layer, which contains a person's true feelings. It is filled with both longing and kindness.)

dialogue.sit: (...I suppose anyone who lives long enough ends up wishing for someone who can't be there. Maybe it's the only way we can feel truly alive.)

dialogue.t: (Time to delve a little deeper...)
Nasha Town is hardly the optimal choice for a place to live, but it has character, and a reasonable population density.
Oh, don't be nervous. I was just thinking where might make a good starting point for your journey.
Perhaps I should send you further afield. Khaenri'ah, perhaps?

dialogue.sit: Khaenri'ah ceased to exist long ago.

dialogue.t: Once again, you fail to understand the possibilities that the Trilune creates. Anything that has existed in the past, I can now recreate.
You simply do not wish to see that happen. That might be because you miss your sibling and fear getting answers that you are not ready to learn... but this is not for me to judge.
If we are to collaborate, we need to maintain an amicable relationship. In a moment, you will be able to...
Hmm?
(Oh no!)
Don't move.
Something unwanted has crept into... Oh? Gone as quickly as it came.
*panting*...
...Did you save me?
If I hadn't cut the connection, Dottore might have caught you from the other side and destroyed you.
This was a good idea, but once is plenty. You were exceptionally brave. Excellent work.
Thanks, but now's not the time for that.
Dodo! Dodo! Dodoco!
Albedo speaking.
I think I know where he(she) is.

dialogue.sit: (I can't see anything, even though my eyes are wide open... But why?)

dialogue.t: Ah, sorry about that.
I take it you didn't notice. Just now, a friend of yours took a little peek into your mind.

dialogue.sit: (...Could it be Nefer? How did she do it? Did she use something as a medium to connect to me?)

dialogue.t: Do you think she's aware of your current circumstances?
Oh dear, have I stunned you into silence? I only wanted to slow down your time a little so I could stop your intruder in her tracks. It would have been nice to capture the spy.
I must say, I'm finding the ability to adjust the flow of time rather intriguing. The moment you closed your eyes, time seemed to grow impossibly viscous, didn't it?
A whole month passed before you opened your eyes again — but only for you. No one else was affected. I daresay this is something only a god can achieve.

dialogue.sit: Point taken. You've proven, once again, that you have god-tier powers.

dialogue.t: Oh, you misunderstand. This wasn't about proving a point — I was testing things out. I find I learn best by doing. And I have to admit, time is not the easiest dimension to control.
I only wanted to make you sleep for a short while, but it ended up lasting a whole month... Clearly, some finesse is required to wield the authority over Time as I wish.
I hope you're not angry with me. It was only a month's discrepancy — nothing too serious. Had I been off by a year, a decade, or even a century... That would have been quite a different story.

dialogue.sit: You could've frozen me for millions of years... So much for collaboration. You aren't showing much sincerity.

dialogue.t: Millions of years? To what end?
I wonder if you don't understand humans all that well. They are very pragmatic creatures who understand only that which they can perceive with their senses.
If I had you sit here for a week, I imagine people might sympathize. But if I left you here for a hundred, a thousand, or ten thousand years...
The sheer size of that number would cause it to lose all meaning to them. They would not have the capacity to comprehend your suffering, and thus they could not empathize.
Unfortunately, while gods do exist in Teyvat, it is ordinary humans that account for most of the population.
Their lifespans are so limited, their bodies so fragile... Did you ever really hope that they could begin to understand someone like you?
Your long life and unique origins make you fundamentally different from them. How long will it be before they start to treat you like the alien you are? Before you are ostracized, outcast?

*sigh* Even I feel bad for you, sometimes. This world has made you into a slave. So many times, you have served its will ... and not once have the powers that be ever thought to grant you the one, simple thing you wish for.
You have been treated most unfairly.
I can change that. I will grant you special privileges, and give you back the status you rightly deserve as a Descender.
(I've entered the past three times at this point, but I still have so many questions...)
(For instance, beyond each point being further back in time than the last, what determines the specific locations at which I can make entry?)
(So far, the common thread linking all three scenarios is that {NICKNAME} has been present...)
(But it's more than that. I know I sensed something familiar around him(her)... What was it?)
(I'll keep this question in mind as I carry on...)
Humans... You never change. Always trying to use powers you neither comprehend nor control.
(This looks like Starsand Shoal... Was this before Rerir regained his physical form?)
You've messed with the cannon again, huh? Sorry, but this round's not gonna go your way!
(The cannon... That's right, I was at Silvermoon Hall and I sensed an abnormal kuuvahki fluctuation coming from Nasha Town.)
(And right after that came an ominous power emanating from Starsand Shoal...)
My body was once torn into countless pieces and hurled into the swirling chaos of time itself. But even so, my life and will were not extinguished.
(I wonder if I could try to prevent his resurrection...)
(But how would I do it? What can I do, here and now...)
{NICKNAME}...
Behind you... Look at that light...
(No! I won't make it in time...!)
(He(She)'s using the kuuvahki shield, like I taught him(her)... Is he(she) gonna use it to block the cannon's beam?)
(He(She)'s strong — I'm sure he(she) can manage. But the force released when the beam impacts the shield might lead to collateral damage...)
(...! Hiisi Island... The Frostmoon Scions will be exposed to lethal levels of kuuvahki...)
A question, if I may, kind Miss Columbina.
When the cannon's kuuvahki beam was deflected earlier, I saw several bolts of energy streak toward Hiisi Island, only to be blocked. Did you also have a hand in that?
Maybe that really was me after all... Well, fut{RUBY#[D]present}ure me. But I don't know if I have enough power left...
Let all mortal flesh keep silent before the light.
(There's no time...!)
As I stood by the door of the Golden House, guarding the eternal flame.
(I have to make it...!)
O Frost Moon, O great land... O, slumbering moonlight of Nod-Krai...
If you can hear me, if you can sense my call... Then please, heed me once more!
Did it... work...?
Hey... Wake up.
Hey! Did you hear me?
Columbina! I said, wake up! Now!
...Hmm? Oh. Good morning, Sandrone.
It's three in the afternoon, actually... And could you kindly not use my quarters as your personal nap room next time?
Aw... But I feel so safe here.
And your... coffee, right? It's so bitter, but it smells lovely.
Hah, it's like you were raised by wolves in a forest or something. What did you drink growing up? Grass tea?
The Frostmoon Scions certainly lead a more frugal existence than the Fatui.
Then I'll bet you've never eaten one of these before!
...It smells delicious.
Hehe, that's because it's a Fontainian recipe. I had a little free time today, so I made a batch.
Rosalyne will be here shortly, but if you really can't wait, I guess you can go ahead and—
*munching*
Hey! At least let me finish before you start eating! Did the Frostmoon Scions not teach you basic table manners!?
Or did the rules not apply to you, because you're the high and mighty Moon Goddess?
Mmm... These are so tasty.
Of course they are. I made them.
I was worried they might contain traces of machine oil.
...What?
...Y'know, there's something I've always wanted to ask you. Why did you leave your old home and join the Fatui?
I mean, I'm sure their food was awful. But there's gotta be more to it than that?
Well... Life there didn't go quite how I imagined.

Surely you can just answer a few prayers here and there in return for the free food and drink? How bad can it be?
Well... Would you help other people, just for free food and drink?
Hmm?
The Doctor told me that you were created by a great mechanic... Lord Something-Fisher...?
The "Lord-Artificer"... Bah, some people can't keep their mouths shut...
Oh, Lord-Artificer. And didn't he have something to do with the, uh, narcissist...?
Narzissenkreuz Ordo.
Yes, that was it. Narzissenkreuz Ordo. So, would you try to fulfill their wishes?
You must be joking. I wouldn't go even if they paid me — I don't even know them.
Exactly. Well, I felt the same way. I did not know the people who made demands of me.
Huh. What do you know? We're on the same page for once.
In his later years, Alain did ask me if there was anything I wanted to do — if I had wishes of my own. Hmph, well, I don't. And I'm not in any mood to fulfill someone else's, either.
...Who's Alain?
He was the... You know what? Never mind. You're not gonna remember. Anyway, the point I'm trying to make is, neither of us is the self-sacrificing type.
Lemme ask you this. What sort of place would you like to live in if you could choose?
Hmm... A place where people don't ask me for things I cannot give them. Where they don't worship me, or fear me, but just want to chat with me like a normal person...
I'd also like the freedom to come and go as I please. And ideally, it would be somewhere with the smell of coffee and snacks...
Hah. Not to burst your bubble, but no such place exists in the world. Now, take your snacks and scram!

Sandrone... {NICKNAME}...

(And... Will I ever find my way back?)
Hey... Wake up.
Hey! Did you hear me?
Columbina! I said, wake up! Now!
...Hmm? Oh. Good morning, Sandrone.
It's three in the afternoon, actually... And could you kindly not use my quarters as your personal nap room next time?
Aw... But I feel so safe here.
And your... coffee, right? It's so bitter, but it smells lovely.
Hah, it's like you were raised by wolves in a forest or something. What did you drink growing up? Grass tea?
The Frostmoon Scions certainly lead a more frugal existence than the Fatui.
Then I'll bet you've never eaten one of these before!
...It smells delicious.
Hehe, that's because it's a Fontainian recipe. I had a little free time today, so I made a batch.
Rosalyne will be here shortly, but if you really can't wait, I guess you can go ahead and—
*munching*
Hey! At least let me finish before you start eating! Did the Frostmoon Scions not teach you basic table manners!?
Or did the rules not apply to you, because you're the high and mighty Moon Goddess?
Mmm... These are so tasty.
Of course they are. I made them.
I was worried they might contain traces of machine oil.
...What?

(The Final Night Cemetery... This is where Flins is based.)
...Or not! How are we supposed to read through this many files!?
Difficult, yes, but it is also our most efficient option.
(Seems like they're searching for information... Oh, I remember. Flins and Varka talked about some files on the Wild Hunt...)
(...Was this my doing, too?)
To expose the true intentions of this Rerir, we need to dive into Nod-Krai's history.
(Are my actions changing the past... or are they simply completing a process?)
(Is all of this inevitable? Or am I the one making these decisions?)
(If I choose not to help them now, will it change how things turn out?)
*sigh* Hope we don't land on our heads, then...
(Haha... They're my friends. I can't not help them...)
Ahh! Gh—Ghost!
(And the other one was... here.)
Hey, another file's moving!
(That should do it...)
Hmm...?
Luonnotar?
You... can sense my presence?
...! Wait!
(Luonnotar... So she's that familiar presence I've been sensing all along!)
(She's always been by {NICKNAME}'s side. That explains why {NICKNAME} has been there each time I've entered the past...)
(But why Luonnotar? Is it because she has a connection to me as the Moon Goddess's familiar? If so, why not any other kuuhenki?)
That's...
(I cannot sense any power up ahead. Just a void, stretching out into infinity...)
(This is likely my final chance to enter the past.)
(It's now or never. I have to find a way back.)
...Hiisi Island? How far back in time is this?
(Where's Luonnotar? I... can't sense her presence this time...)
Seeing Ineffa and Aino reunited like that sure was heart-warming...
...! {NICKNAME}, Paimon!
(No, stay calm... I don't have much power left to change things. I don't even have that much time left here.)
(Think, Columbina. How do I find a way back?)
A way back... to where?
(Do I... go back to Moon-Prayer Night? Or to the future that followed?)
(And if I return in my current state, what will become of me then?)
(Dottore's actions that day prove that he'd been planning that for a long time. He had already seized the power of two Moon Marrows before capturing me...)
(Even if I manage to get back, how can I fight against him when he wields the trilune authority?)
(...I can't. If I go back like this, I'll be playing right into his hands.)
(I have to find some way of rivaling the power he has usurped...)
Hmm? Wait, time flowing backwards... The trilune authority...
...! Does that mean... I think I know what the final destination of this lunar reflection might be.
...I know what I must do.
Speaking of homes, we must already be close to where the Frostmoon Scions live. The vibe here feels different, just like the scenery...
(But how do I communicate my plan to my friends?)
(Should I write it down here? No, someone else will see it...)
(I need something with a close connection to me... Something I can use as a medium to tell them what's happened to me in here...)
Haha... Now it makes sense...
Hey, what was that? Felt like some sort of breeze blew by, and then the petals suddenly turned into... Eh?
(It was I who brought Luonnotar into being... I gave up a piece of my own soul to create her.)
(That's why I could sense a familiar power from the moment I entered this space...)
(It also explains why she's been present in every past location that I've entered...)
(Because we have a deep connection.)
Hey there! What's your name?
(And the reason why there are no more gates to the past after this point is that Luonnotar hadn't been born then...)
Hehe... No wonder I sensed the trace of a blessing when we first met, but I still didn't recognize the soul hidden within you.
Back then, I was just a little lost dove... I had yet to become Columbina Hyposelenia...
Go on, go on now... We've got stuff to do. Best you find someone else to hang out with...
I'll be counting on you.
Remember to stay by {NICKNAME}'s side. Guide him(her), and help him(her) in my stead...
Oh, and bring him(her) to the garden where the Moon-Prayer Blossoms grow. There's a little lost dove there who will need his(her) help.
Haha... Go on.
You too... Go, and live your story.
As for mine... Mine must go in a different direction...
How would you like to experience the thrill of never being held accountable for your actions? You could crush people like ants without consequence. Or tear off their heads, or limbs, as you please.
Believe me, such a life is but one small step away.

dialogue.sit: (What point is he trying to make? Freedom? But... the freedom to kill? To do evil and get away with it?)
Why would you offer me that?

dialogue.t: The creation of a world is the ultimate scientific experiment. I have taken my research to the highest level, where I shall be not just a god, but also a servant to many sacred spirits. I shall heed the truth and perform holy deeds.
A god's laboratory is the perfect playground — but it needs the right occupant to explore its full potential.

Mortals are found everywhere one looks. Not so with Descenders. I'd prefer my first guest to be a distinguished individual such as yourself, and I know you could make the most of the opportunities it offers.

dialogue.sit: (So the condition for entering the new world is to take innocent lives. The same dilemma that Rerir once faced.)
(Could I really bring myself to kill others for my own benefit? Rerir did... and look where it got him.)

dialogue.t: Have you made up your mind?

dialogue.sit: Your playground is no place for me — you're putting your hopes in the wrong person. But we both know I'm not quite the hero you say I am either. I have my own reasons for the journey I'm on, and they aren't all selfless.

dialogue.t: You've grown a lot since we last met, but there are still things you are unwilling to compromise on. This will only hinder you.
Why don't I lower my requirements a little, as a gesture of goodwill? I'll give you a little time to learn to be a less noble soul. That'll make things much easier for you.

dialogue.sit: ...I... I really doubt I could live that sort of life.

dialogue.t: And yet you already sound less defiant than a moment ago. The benefits appeal to you, because you can read the signs of the times.
Why don't we return to my research facility? Your last visit was so rushed. There is much that I have yet to show you.
*panting*

dialogue.sit: Hat Guy? How did you get here?

dialogue.t: You're still gonna call me "Hat Guy" after that, huh?

dialogue.sit: You came all this way just to save me?

dialogue.t: I didn't see anyone else in there who needed saving.

dialogue.sit: Fair point. You just caught me by surprise... Thank you.

dialogue.t: Ugh... *cough*
It's nothing. I'll be fine.
Why are you looking at me like that? Is it that shocking that I'd come to your rescue?

dialogue.sit: I'm more shocked that you caught The Doctor off guard...

dialogue.t: I owed you a favor from back in Sumeru. Now, we're even.
Distracting Dottore was tough, I won't lie...
He's not gonna fall for the same trick twice. That was my one shot... I'd hoped to use it to take him out.
Ugh. I never wanted to obliterate someone more than I do right now.
Dottore doesn't recognize me, but his Segments were originally made based on an analysis of my operational principles.
I expect it's only a matter of time before he figures out what I am.

dialogue.sit: (So Dottore doesn't recognize {REALNAME[ID(1)|HOSTONLY(true)]}, because he deleted himself from Irminsul.)
(...Did he really miss his only chance for revenge by saving me?)

dialogue.t: Why the long face? Hey, I'm not blaming you, okay?
And I'm not complaining either. Rescuing you and killing Dottore are equally important goals.
Everyone would be pretty stuck without you. It's best you live to fight another day.
How are you holding up? Are you alright?
Hat Guy said to put safety first, so we agreed to run as far away as we could after leaving the energy field, and only meet up once it was safe.
You don't look injured. It seems that Dottore didn't do anything to you.
Alright, rescue operation complete. Let's head back.
There's a lot more work to be done before this is over.
